title: GraphQL field memoization + adaptive prefix/KV cache cleanup
creator: Diego Holt
description: Motivation: Console backend Aggregator paths are a major source of tail latency and CPU waste due to repeated GraphQL resolver work and noisy prefix/KV cache churn. This ticket consolidates a two-pronged cleanup: (1) introduce scoped, field-level memoization for expensive resolvers to avoid recomputation across identical request shapes; (2) replace ad-hoc prefix eviction in the in-memory KV cache with an adaptive LRU+hot-key protection policy and clear ownership boundaries to reduce cross-request interference. Scope: - Implement a resolver-level memoization util (configurable TTL + key hashing) and apply it to user/route heavy resolvers identified in profiling. - Rework KV cache eviction: add access frequency tracking, hot-key pinning, and per-tenant namespaces. - Add instrumentation (prometheus metrics + tracing spans) for memoization hit-rate, cache eviction rate, and per-resolver compute time. - Benchmark p50/p95/P99 improvements on staging load tests; prepare canary rollout. Out of scope: global CDN cache changes, client-side caching, schema changes. Risks & trade-offs: memoization reduces compute but increases memory; TTL selection is critical for freshness. Adaptive eviction reduces noisy evictions but adds bookkeeping overhead. We'll monitor memory pressure and CPU trade-offs in the canary. Success criteria: - 25% reduction in p95 response time for /api/consoles aggregate endpoints under synthetic load, - Memoization hit-rate >= 30% for targeted resolvers, - No increase in error rate or cache-related tail spikes during canary. Deliverables: design RFC link, implementation PRs, load test results, rollout plan and dashboard panels for monitoring.
